items.title: Nasdaq’s 23-Hour Trading Push Could Turn Global Liquidity Into a Growth Engine
items.summary: Nasdaq plans to launch 23-hour trading on Dec. 6, aiming to capture overseas order flow, boosted by its LeveL Markets acquisition and growing financial technology and compliance software revenue.

items.title: What to Know About Nasdaq President Nelson Griggs Selling 3,226 Shares for $310,212
items.summary: Griggs retains 201,775 shares in direct holdings, with additional exposure through restricted stock units and performance-based equity awards.

items.title: Market Minute 8-18-26- Bonds Keep Bleeding, Yields Keep Rising
items.summary: Equities sagged into the close yesterday, and they remain under pressure today thanks to a continuing selloff in government bonds. Crude oil is modestly higher, while gold, silver, and crypto are slightly lower.

items.title: Nasdaq plans nearly 23-hour trading day from December
items.summary: Investing.com -- Nasdaq is planning to extend trading on its U.S. stock market to nearly 23 hours a day, five days a week, as it seeks to meet rising global demand for U.S. equities.

items.title: Cboe Global Stock Falls 22% in 3 Months: Time to Buy the Dip?
items.summary: Cboe Global's 22% slide contrasts with stronger growth prospects, recurring revenues and an affordable valuation, supporting the case to buy the dip.

items.title: Tokenization Promises To Break Trading Barriers. What Investors Need To Know.
items.summary: Tokenization promises to boost liquidity, cut transaction costs and offer fractional shares, as well as enable 24/7 trading and immediate trade settlements.

items.title: Will Nasdaq's (NDAQ) LeveL Markets Deal and Digital Liquidity Push Redefine Its Market Role?
items.summary: Nasdaq recently entered a definitive agreement to acquire all equity interests of LeveL Markets, a U.S. Alternative Trading System, to broaden its institutional trading and always-on digital liquidity capabilities. The deal, paired with the creation of a Digital Liquidity Networks unit led by Roland Chai, highlights Nasdaq’s push into more connected, institutional-grade market infrastructure.
